flags.reason: The guide and its evidence were checked on 20 October on 0.1.78-c7d3348 and not re-checked on the installed build, dbe0e02, which changed SummaryTile for #352: children left out shows no action (no placeholder Button), onActionPress with actionLabel adds the built-in small secondary Button, a Button or IconButton in children is AppearanceBrand Secondary and Button / Size S without modes on the tile, the description stays on one line and ends in … like the title (disableTruncation lets both wrap), and a tile without onPress is named by its title. This entry follows the installed package and leaves out the guide sentences dbe0e02 contradicts (listed in its notes): the placeholder Button (Configuration, States, the Your own Button pair, Sources), setting AppearanceBrand Secondary and Button / Size S on the tile (Configuration, the Modes on the tile pair, Sources), the description that wraps and never truncates (Anatomy, Sizing, Content), and disableTruncation affecting only the title and the static tile not announced by its title (Sources). Re-extract once #352 is closed and the guide is re-checked and published. Added by Claude Code in the overnight run agentpack-batch11, for Marcin to confirm.

configuration.text: There is no default action: pass a Button or an IconButton in children, or use actionLabel and onActionPress for the built-in small secondary Button.

onActionPress, with children left out and no onPress on the tile, renders the built-in small secondary Button with that handler instead of a dead placeholder; a tile with onPress has no built-in Button.

actionLabel labels the built-in Button only when children is left out, onActionPress is set and the tile has no onPress; without actionLabel the Button reads “Button”, and actionLabel on its own renders no button.
The tile passes its modes to whatever you put there, and your Button’s own modes win.

examples.purpose: Spending on the Money screen, the guide’s In context: the tile heads a card and the list under it is the block it introduces. See all does the work through its own onPress (the empty handler stands for opening the screen’s spending view). The tile carries no modes: on the installed package a Button in children starts at AppearanceBrand Secondary and Button / Size S. The guide’s MoneyValue amounts are left out because MoneyValue has no entry in this pack.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <SummaryTile title="Spending" description="Your top categories this month" confidence="High">
      <Button label="See all" onPress={() => {}} />
    </SummaryTile>
    <ListGroup>
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" navArrow={false} title="Food" supportText="12 orders" />
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" navArrow={false} title="Shopping" supportText="5 orders" />
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" navArrow={false} title="Travel" supportText="3 trips" />
    </ListGroup>
  </VStack>
</Card>

props.name: title
props.description: 16 px, weight 700, drawn on a 20 px line (its token says 18). Declared: Bold heading shown at the top-left of the tile. Default "Spending", from the component source.

props.name: description
props.description: 12 px, weight 500, on a 16 px line. Declared: Smaller supporting copy rendered beneath the title. Default "Know your spending and savings", from the component source.

props.name: confidence
props.description: A number is bucketed to the nearest level: above 5/6 High, above 1/2 Medium, above 1/6 Low, otherwise None. Declared: Confidence level for the inline `StrengthIndicator` next to the title. Defaults to `'None'` to match the Figma reference (all bars unlit). Pass `null` to hide the indicator entirely. Default "None", from the component source.

props.name: chevron
props.description: When `true`, render a trailing forward chevron (`NavArrow`) — the convention for "tap the tile to drill in" affordance. Defaults to `false`. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: children
props.description: Action slot rendered to the right of the text content. There is no default control — pass a `Button` / `IconButton` here, or use `actionLabel` / `onActionPress` for the built-in small secondary button. A slotted `Button` / `IconButton` starts at AppearanceBrand Secondary and Button / Size S. Modes on the tile override those defaults. The child's own `modes` override the tile.

props.name: actionLabel
props.description: Label for the built-in action button. Used only when `children` is omitted and `onActionPress` is set. Defaults to `'Button'` in that case. `actionLabel` on its own does not render a button.

props.name: onActionPress
props.description: Press handler for the built-in action button. When set (and `children` is omitted) the tile renders a small secondary button instead of a dead placeholder.

props.name: onPress
props.description: The row dims to 0.7 opacity while pressed. Declared: Optional press handler for the entire tile. When provided, the tile is wrapped in a `Pressable`, gets `accessibilityRole="button"` and the built-in action button is suppressed so the rendered HTML doesn't contain a `<button>` inside another `<button>`. Pair this with `chevron` for the navigational tile pattern. An explicit `children` node is still rendered — do not pass a `Button` there.

props.name: modes
props.description: The tile’s own tokens have one mode: an 8 px gap between the text and the action, no padding, 8 px between the title row and the description, and 4 px between the title and the meter. No mode changes them. Declared: Design token modes for theming (e.g. `{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }`).

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, the title and description wrap instead of ellipsizing. By default both are clamped to one line.
